history.dynasty: Maratha (temple built during the reign of Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj of Satara)
history.period: Established 1738; deity shifted from Quelossim (Cavellossim) after the Portuguese destroyed the original temple in 1564; 450th year completed 4 Dec 2016
history.summary: The Kavlem shrine of Shantadurga (Santeri), the goddess who, per legend, mediated a battle between Vishnu and Shiva — she is shown holding two serpents, one in each hand, representing the two gods, and is the kuldevi of many Goud Saraswat Brahmin families. The original temple at Cavellossim (Quelossim) in Salcete was destroyed by the Portuguese in 1564; the deity was shifted to Kavlem, and the present temple was built during the reign of Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj of Satara (established 1738). The complex fuses Indo-Portuguese architecture: pyramid-shaped shikharas, Roman-arched windows with stained glass, a flat dome, maroon-peach-white paint, Kashmir-stone pillars and floors, a huge tank, a deepastambha and a golden palanquin used on festive occasions. The Kavale Math (Gaudapadacharya Math) provides spiritual headship to the saunsthan.

name: Shri Shantadurga Temple
town_description: Kavlem (Kavalem) is a village in Ponda taluka, North Goa, about 30 km from Panaji at the foothill of a mountain chain. Part of the Ponda temple belt where many deities were sheltered during the Portuguese era, it is set amid lush greenery and also hosts the Shri Gaudapadacharya (Kavale) Math.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism - Santeri/Shantadurga as mediator of Vishnu and Shiva)
